A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural Atlas Graphs work, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v2 additionally includes supplementary Sections A–D. The retained content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 report original Waymo and DAVIS reconstruction results in Tables 1–3, alongside scene decomposition and editing demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original evaluations and adds temporal-quality measurements, large-camera-motion tests, component ablations, additional baseline comparisons, and measured training times.

M1.justification: The plane-node representation, spline flow, view-dependent fields, compositing, and photometric/mask objective remain unchanged. Section 3.6 and Appendix A expand texture-mapping, camera-refinement, and staged-training specifications as additional method details; they do not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: The seven main Waymo segments and 15 DAVIS sequences are retained. Appendix C adds two large-ego-motion Waymo sequences, s-191 and s-254, and corrupted-mask and bounding-box-mask scenarios. These provide a focused extension of camera-motion and input-quality conditions within the existing domains.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates OmniRe and EmerNeRF on Waymo, and OmnimatteRF and Layered Neural Atlases on DAVIS. v2 retains these and evaluates Street Gaussians, Periodic Vibration Gaussian, and Deformable 3D Gaussians on the main Waymo subset in Tables 14–15, substantially expanding the comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds FVD and T-LPIPS evaluation on selected Waymo/DAVIS sequences, T-LPIPS and FID assessment of decomposition and texture edits, and controlled model-size, component-removal, motion-granularity, and mask experiments. These introduce substantial evaluation procedures beyond v1's reconstruction metrics and qualitative edits. Appendix B's newly disclosed resolutions and preprocessing do not establish changes to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: v1 contains no component ablation study. v2 adds systematic capacity, initialization, flow, view-dependence, pose, and mask ablations in Table 13; large-camera-motion robustness tests; and qualitative mask-failure analyses in Figures 10–12. Temporal editing analyses and additional manipulation examples further expand diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates only. v2 introduces standard deviations and aggregation descriptions across frames, objects, or subsequences in Tables 6–10 and 14–15. This substantially expands variability reporting, but does not establish repeated training runs, seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals, or formal significance testing.

E6.justification: Corresponding Waymo tables revise numerous values: OmniRe's mean PSNR changes from 36.92 to 36.78, and NAG's vehicle/human mean PSNR changes from 42.69/42.89 to 42.88/42.94. DAVIS Table 3 is numerically unchanged. Extensive new results cover temporal quality, ablations, additional baselines, and timing. Under the newly tested large-motion scenario, Table 12 reports 32.02 dB for NAG versus 33.17 for OmniRe on s-191.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds explicit camera-ray, intrinsic/extrinsic, and spline-based camera-pose definitions in Equations 10–13 that were not stated in v1. This is a limited expansion of mathematical specification, without new theorems or proofs. Main Equations 1–8 remain unchanged, and Equation 9 merely displays the existing texture-blending formula.

C1.justification: The hybrid representation, editability, and cross-domain contribution claims remain intact. The introduction narrows the approximately 5 dB Waymo comparison to object-specific 3DGS methods. The conclusion revises actor gains from 11.5 dB for both classes to 11.2 for vehicles and 10.7 for humans.

C2.justification: v1 already discusses planarity, initialization, and large-motion limitations. v2 explicitly excludes novel-view synthesis and accurate 3D reconstruction, explains background flow collapse under large camera motion, and distinguishes stable reconstruction scores from degraded occluded-object decomposition under poor masks. Appendix C.2 also discusses unavailable editing ground truth and limitations of quality proxies, substantially refining applicability and interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B newly document the phased 80-epoch schedule, Adam settings, MLP/hash-grid architecture, parameter counts, initialization, exact Waymo subsequence ranges, and DAVIS preprocessing and resolution differences. Hardware, measured training times, and project/video access instructions are added; the repository link already existed. These substantially expand reproducibility information, although the ray budgets stated in B.3 and C.7 conflict.

R1.justification: The main related-work section is largely retained, but Appendix D substantially expands positioning through 2D/2.5D/3D and object-specific/object-agnostic comparisons, including tradeoffs between geometric expressivity, required priors, and editing. Added references cover the additional Gaussian-splatting comparators, RoDynRF, and video-quality assessment; Appendix C.2 critically discusses existing evaluation approaches.

P1.justification: v2 adds an extensive explanatory structure with a supplementary introduction, contents page, organized method and experimental details, and a comparative scene-representation discussion. Section 3.6 is expanded to explain reference-image projection, flow inversion, and atlas-space editing. Although much of the main narrative remains intact, the added exposition is substantial; acknowledgments, affiliation, and conference-header text also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds the counterfactual-editing Figure 5 and supplementary Figures 6–18 covering masks, failures, ablations, comparisons, and edits. Tables 4–16 introduce implementation summaries and new results, with Tables 6–8 redisplaying main results alongside standard deviations. Retained figures and tables are also relocated as the main text reflows.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1's supplied evidence: Appendices A–B substantially improve reproducibility, while Appendix C validates component choices, expands comparisons, and tests failure conditions. The large-motion and mask studies make the method's practical boundaries more credible. Conflicting ray-budget descriptions and reliance on temporal proxies remain weaknesses, but the gains in transparency, empirical support, and interpretation constitute a substantial overall improvement.
